authors: Twan ten Haaf and Peter J. M. Weijs

basis: Article copyright and unrestricted supporting-data statement
rights.scope: Local reproducible analysis; publish original aggregate results and metadata only. Do not relicense third-party data as MIT.

columns.Measured_REE_kJ: Resting Energy Expenditure (MJ/day) measured by indirect calorimetry

unitAudit.referenceLabel: Resting Energy Expenditure (MJ/day) measured by indirect calorimetry

unitDecision: Raw reference is kJ/day despite MJ/day label; divide by 4.184. Reference-only mean divided by 1000 matches the published rounded 7.68 MJ/day within 0.01 MJ/day. Inference disclosed before prediction.
sexMapping: File Gender labels 0=Female, 1=Male map to the historical equation parameter only; do not infer identity or clinical applicability.

measurement.calibration: Daily two standard gases and volume; automatic recalibration every five minutes
measurement.preparation: No vigorous exercise for 12 hours; no food/beverages except water for four hours; at least 30 minutes laboratory rest
measurement.selection: 30-minute recording; first five minutes discarded; steady-state CV <10%; authors excluded nine ovulation-phase and four RER-out-of-range participants
measurement.bodyComposition: BODPOD; thoracic gas volume estimated in 31 participants; individual estimate flag not supplied

independence.cohort: Different from the prior 2023 body-composition cohort and the original Mifflin/Cunningham development populations.
independence.equations: Fixed published equations; no fit on this evaluation cohort. Ten Haaf new equations are in-sample developments and excluded.
independence.knownOutcomes: Published conclusion favoring Cunningham and poor Mifflin ±10% accuracy was already read during H2-B. Not an unseen confirmatory trial.
independence.reviewer: Same maintaining agent; independent implementation is not independent personnel.

limits: Selected Dutch recreational athletes aged 18–35; no clinical population coverage.
Four-hour fast differs from stricter overnight basal protocols.
Within-person identifiers across older unrelated publications cannot be exhaustively verified.
No TDEE, repeated personal calibration, injury, diet or training outcome.
